quest.title: Guests in Qingce
quest.description: Wang'ya has something to say to you at Wangshu Inn...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Hero's Wit x2, Mora x20000

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: That should be enough...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you going to do?

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Hmm? I'm surprised to see you here...

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: You still remember how I invited Qingzhou and Mr. Bohuan to Qingce Village, right?

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: They've headed there already. Meet them there if you want to join.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: I still have something to do here. I'll make my way to Qingce Village as soon as I'm done.

choices.text: I feel like you're never done...

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: Ah... I can't help it. The workload at the Ministry of Civil Affairs during the Lantern Rite is unbelievable.

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: The Ministry of Civil Affairs is transporting some festival supplies today, and Wangshu Inn happens to be a transit station.

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: Since I'm here, I promised them that I'd monitor the transfer of goods...

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: You can go to Qingce Village first and wait for their arrival. Making an inventory shouldn't take me long.

choices.text: I feel like you're constantly busy during the festival season...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Mm... Not bad! In fact, your calligraphy is the best I've ever seen.

dialogues.speaker: Mr. Bohuan
dialogues.text: Hahaha, that's very nice of you to say! I'm afraid that's the best I can do... Would you like anything else written?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I see that you're all set up.

dialogues.speaker: Mr. Bohuan
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you! I just got here. My calligraphy is actually in great demand. I need to pick up my pace if I want to assist all those people.

dialogues.speaker: Mr. Bohuan
dialogues.text: Qingzhou is here too. Have you seen him since you came?

response.speaker: Mr. Bohuan
response.text: Uh... We traveled to Qingce Village together, but he seemed very perturbed all the way here.

response.speaker: Mr. Bohuan
response.text: I asked what troubled him, but he only sighed and said he lost inspiration.

response.speaker: Mr. Bohuan
response.text: When we finally got here, I got straight to writing, and he said he wanted to look around alone, so we parted ways.

response.speaker: Mr. Bohuan
response.text: Perhaps the villagers know where he is. You'd better ask around.

response.speaker: Mr. Bohuan
response.text: While you're at it, I could use your help with returning these adorned Xiao Lanterns to their owners. Let me mark their locations for you...

response.speaker: Mr. Bohuan
response.text: I still have a lot of writing to do here, so I'll leave the lantern delivery to you.

talks.objective: Give a Xiao Lantern to Uncle Ghast

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Ghast
dialogues.text: What is it, youngster?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Xiao Lanterns with Mr. Bohuan's calligraphy...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Ghast
dialogues.text: Oh... Right, I did ask that gentleman to make an inscription for me. That's it, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Ghast
dialogues.text: Nicely done... Thank you for bringing it to me. I still need to thank that calligrapher, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you seen Qingzhou by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Ghast
dialogues.text: Qingzhou... Do you mean that famous poet? I saw him around here with a huge frown on his face. He seemed really upset.

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Ghast
dialogues.text: Uh... That's all I know. Maybe someone else will be able to point you to him.

talks.objective: Give a Xiao Lantern to Master Lu

dialogues.speaker: Master Lu
dialogues.text: Welcome to Fanmu Carpenter's! Anything you'd like to order?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Xiao Lanterns with Mr. Bohuan's calligraphy...

dialogues.speaker: Master Lu
dialogues.text: It's done? Let me take a look...

dialogues.speaker: Master Lu
dialogues.text: That's quite something! A fine piece of writing!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you seen Qingzhou by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Master Lu
dialogues.text: Ah, that poet? I saw him earlier with some kids who were following him around.

dialogues.speaker: Master Lu
dialogues.text: I wish I could tell you more. Perhaps other villagers will be of more help.

talks.objective: Give a Xiao Lantern to Hanfeng

dialogues.speaker: Hanfeng, "Cold Blade"
dialogues.text: Hello. Can I help you with something?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Xiao Lanterns with Mr. Bohuan's calligraphy...

dialogues.speaker: Hanfeng, "Cold Blade"
dialogues.text: Is it ready? Let me see...

dialogues.speaker: Hanfeng, "Cold Blade"
dialogues.text: Oh my! This is lovely! That gentleman is blessed with amazing talent...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you seen Qingzhou by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Hanfeng, "Cold Blade"
dialogues.text: Qingzhou? Yes, I've seen him. He just passed by here with a bunch of children.

dialogues.speaker: Hanfeng, "Cold Blade"
dialogues.text: He said... that they were going out to play some games. Odd, isn't it? You wouldn't expect such a renowned poet to entertain children that way...

dialogues.speaker: Hanfeng, "Cold Blade"
dialogues.text: You shouldn't have too much trouble finding him. Just go that way.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: This... will not work. It needs to be more elaborate...

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: No... Another dead end. Something so cryptic would only alienate my little audience...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you up to?

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you, my liege! I am crafting lantern riddles for these children.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lantern... what?

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: You are not familiar with those, I presume? You may consider it... a game, of sorts.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Each Xiao Lantern has a short riddle inscribed upon it. The person who solves the riddle can take the lantern it was written on.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: At present, I am trying to perfect these three riddles. And as if this wasn't enough, my little friends also insist on adding additional "loot" for correct solutions...

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Hehe, "loot"... How do they even know of such expressions?

choices.text: What about your competition with Vermeer?

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: The competition... *sigh* It shames me to say this... The matter has been on my mind ever since we agreed upon it...

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: But no matter where I look, I cannot seem to find even an ounce of inspiration. I have no idea what kind of poem would be a worthy depiction of both Liyue Harbor and the Lantern Rite...

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Truth be told, that was the reason why I accepted Wang'ya's invitation. I had hoped that maybe here I'd collect some material and find my muse.

choices.text: Are the lantern riddles supposed to help you with that?

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Hahaha, do not worry about me, my liege. My writer's block has not got the best of me just yet.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Those lantern riddles, however, have nothing to do with finding inspiration.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: I felt really bad for these children. They have no one to entertain them or take them on a holiday outing in this place, completely bereft of any festive atmosphere as it is...

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: I just wanted to amuse them with my riddles so that they can participate in the Lantern Rite like the rest of us.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Anyways, I just came up with three riddles. Now I just need three Xiao Lanterns...

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Would you be kind enough to bring me three sets of Xiao Lantern materials, my liege?

choices.text: What kind of material could you possibly find here?
Still remember your competition with Vermeer?

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Hmm, you are most capable indeed! I just need a moment to make those lanterns. Then, we can write the riddles on them.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Alright, this should do it.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Heh... I'm from Liyue after all. Making Xiao Lanterns runs in our blood. Although my technique isn't the greatest...

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Our little friends are ready to take their shot at the riddles. Why don't you stay and cheer for them?

choices.text: Who knew you had it in you...

talks.objective: Give three Xiao Lantern materials to Qingzhou

dialogues.speaker: Lantern Riddle
dialogues.text: "Rock-hard flesh and bamboo bones. Lives in the city with thousands of clones."

dialogues.speaker: Lantern Riddle
dialogues.text: "Pitch-black sea marks the end of its flight. Within its body hides resplendent light."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Th—That's what a lantern riddle is? Too difficult for Paimon's little brain... Do you have any clue what the answer might be?

dialogues.speaker: Lantern Riddle
dialogues.text: "Rock-hard flesh and bamboo bones. Lives in the city with thousands of clones."

dialogues.speaker: Lantern Riddle
dialogues.text: "Pitch-black sea marks the end of its flight. Within its body hides resplendent light."

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Hmm... Wrong answer. You may wish to give it some more thought.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Correct! You've guessed right.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Xiao Lanterns have bamboo frames and insides made of rocks. They float in the sky after release. You do not find them in the wild, and that's why each one "lives in the city."

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Even though the chunk of Plaustrite inside is not easily damaged, the lampshade can break. Once released, a Xiao Lantern may fall into the sea, which "marks the end of its flight."

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Even so, the wishes committed to the lanterns will not perish... Which is symbolized by their "resplendent light."

response.speaker: Little Liu
response.text: *sigh* I wouldn't have thought about it at all...

response.speaker: Little Liu
response.text: Wow, you're so smart! So... you should take this gift!

response.speaker: Little Liu
response.text: My friends say that you should always get some "loot" for guessing the right answer... This can be your "loot."

dialogues.speaker: Lantern Riddle
dialogues.text: "A bamboo tube with powdered stone. Burns in the night as bright as the sun."

dialogues.speaker: Lantern Riddle
dialogues.text: "It roars like thunder, very frightening. But it summons ash instead of lightning."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This one seems really simple. If you think hard enough...

dialogues.speaker: Lantern Riddle
dialogues.text: "A bamboo tube with powdered stone. Burns in the night as bright as the sun."

dialogues.speaker: Lantern Riddle
dialogues.text: "It roars like thunder, very frightening. But it summons ash instead of lightning."

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Hmm... Wrong answer. You may wish to give it some more thought.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Correct! You've guessed right. Haha, it must have been a fairly simple one. Bamboo tube, powdered stone, burns in the night...

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: And then, "roars like thunder." "Firecrackers" is the only possible answer.

response.speaker: Little Zuo
response.text: ...Ohhhh! Of course!!! How did I not get that...

response.speaker: Little Zuo
response.text: Since you solved the riddle, here's your reward.

dialogues.speaker: Lantern Riddle
dialogues.text: "Watch me rise from Wanmin and ride the wind to Jueyun."

dialogues.speaker: Lantern Riddle
dialogues.text: "But if my string is broken, I flail and plummet to oblivion."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... What does that mean?

dialogues.speaker: Lantern Riddle
dialogues.text: "Watch me rise from Wanmin and ride the wind to Jueyun."

dialogues.speaker: Lantern Riddle
dialogues.text: "But if my string is broken, I flail and plummet to oblivion."

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Hmm... Wrong answer. You may wish to give it some more thought.

choices.text: An adventurer using a wind glider.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Correct! You've guessed right. You have to "ride the wind" if you want to get as high as Jueyun...

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: And you control it with a string. So naturally, it must be a kite.

response.speaker: Little You
response.text: What? How does that work... Hmm...

response.speaker: Little You
response.text: ...Oh, I guess it must be. How did you get that, though? You must be super smart.

response.speaker: Little You
response.text: Since you solved the riddle, here's your reward.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: You must have a sharp mind if you managed to solve all three riddles.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Um, so... Although typically the one who solves the riddles gets free Xiao Lanterns, I'm afraid I simply can't give you these Xiao Lanterns here...

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: And it would ruin my hands if I were to try and make three more. Ahem... Please take these instead.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: These children don't seem ready to stop just yet... It seems like three riddles was not enough. I'll have to come up with a few more.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Oh, don't read too much into it... That was just a little idea I came up with, it's nothing serious.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: But these children are waiting very expectantly for me to give them lantern riddles.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: I'll keep entertaining them until they've had enough. When the painter comes, I'll let him know.

response.speaker: Qingzhou
response.text: Ah, would you look at the time? Wang'ya should be arriving any moment now. Please, could you receive her on my behalf? I shall continue entertaining these children with lantern riddles.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Well, I'm here... Traveler? Have you seen Qingzhou and Mr. Bohuan?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Qingzhou and Mr. Bohuan...

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: I see... Great! I thought that nobody would make arrangements if I wasn't here.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: The Ministry of Civil Affairs has quite a lot of goods for distribution. It's taken me a long time to count them all up.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: I came here as soon as I finished. Didn't think I'd end up being so late...

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: But from the sounds of it, everything's under control and I don't need to do anything.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: I'll go and see them in a bit. Let's take a walk first.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Qingce Village... I actually came here as a child a few times.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: I always liked the tofu here, and the little wooden carvings.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: The surroundings here are quite beautiful, too. In the past, a lot of people thought it was great living here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So... what happened?

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Well... for older people, Qingce Village is a calm and easygoing place to live. Everything is familiar, and things don't change much.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Stay here a while and you might even start wondering whether time has stopped.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: But it's maybe not the best place for young people...

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: For a variety of reasons, most of the young people from Qingce Village have moved to Liyue Harbor, leaving only the old people and young children behind.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What reasons, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: It's a long story. Hard to explain.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Let's keep walking.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: To sum up, for one reason or another, Qingce Village has slowly become a village for the elderly and for the kids.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: When the festive season comes around, it's difficult for them to create a really celebratory atmosphere here. The Ministry of Civil Affairs always arranges to send supplies over, but...

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: But that's really all we can do for them as outsiders here.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: I think that what they really need is the company of their families.

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Without your family around you... all the material wealth, all the organized entertainment in the world is just...

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: Ah! Sorry, it's just I deal with things like this all the time... I guess when I'm not careful, I just start talking about heavy topics...

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: On the bright side, Qingce Village is much more festive than usual this year with Qingzhou, Mr. Bohuan, and you here.

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: Thanks again for your help, Traveler.

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: I... It can't be helped. The Ministry of Civil Affairs delivers supplies to many places during the Lantern Rite, and I still have my part to do...

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: Some of the places are so far away that I'll bet you've never even heard of them.

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: And it's not just me. Many of my colleagues are out delivering Xiao Lanterns, too.

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: Our hope and our duty is to deliver Xiao Lanterns to all, so everyone can experience the festival spirit.

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: But as for me... Haha, I'm a bit of an exception. I don't get to go home during the festive period.

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: In a good year, I get to take a few days off near the end of the festival and spend some time with my family.

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: They're generally very understanding about it. But I suspect that this time, my mother's going to nag me about it.

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: Well, I'll have to get back to work shortly. You should make the most of everything going on during the festival.

response.speaker: Wang'ya
response.text: Happy Lantern Rite!

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Have you collected three sets of Xiao Lantern materials yet?

dialogues.speaker: Little Liu
dialogues.text: Ugh, this is soooo haaaard...

dialogues.speaker: Little Liu
dialogues.text: Ohh, so it was Xiao Lanterns. But what the heck are the "Verses of Equilibrium"...

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: Bamboo tube... powdered stone... What does it mean?

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: Firecrackers! How did I not think of that...

dialogues.speaker: Little You
dialogues.text: Hmm, string... Where does that fit in...

dialogues.speaker: Little You
dialogues.text: Ohhhh, a kite...

dialogues.speaker: Wang'ya
dialogues.text: Hmm, I wonder if Qingzhou and Mr. Bohuan have made it to Qingce Village yet...

dialogues.speaker: Granny Ruoxin
dialogues.text: Many thanks for your wonderful calligraphy, a good calligrapher is hard to come by.

dialogues.speaker: Mr. Bohuan
dialogues.text: Why, it's my pleasure! I still have a few more lanterns to do, hold on...

dialogues.speaker: Little Liu
dialogues.text: Ugh, what's the answer to the riddle... I can't get it...

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: Wah, this riddle's too hard for me...

dialogues.speaker: Little You
dialogues.text: So... confused...

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Heh, come on, keep thinking. Once you crack one bit of it, the rest will follow straight away.

dialogues.speaker: Little Liu
dialogues.text: One more, one more! I'll definitely get it this time!

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: This time... This time I'll crack it, too.

dialogues.speaker: Little You
dialogues.text: And I... also wanna try.

dialogues.speaker: Qingzhou
dialogues.text: Okay, children, settle down. Let me think for a moment... Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Uncle Ghast
dialogues.text: Whoa, that's some fine calligraphy...

dialogues.speaker: Hanfeng, "Cold Blade"
dialogues.text: If you're looking for Qingzhou, head out that way. He took some children out to play a game.

dialogues.speaker: Master Lu
dialogues.text: Wow, nice calligraphy...

dialogues.speaker: Little Liu
dialogues.text: I wonder what Uncle Qingzhou's next riddle will be...

dialogues.speaker: Little Zuo
dialogues.text: I'm definitely gonna solve this one.

dialogues.speaker: Little You
dialogues.text: I... I'll try my hardest...
